short: The world's first four-engine aircraft and the first dedicated strategic heavy bomber.
full:
Designed by Igor Sikorsky and introduced in 1914, the Ilya Muromets was originally conceived as a luxurious passenger aircraft before the outbreak of the First World War. When repurposed by the Imperial Russian Air Service, it became the first four-engine strategic bomber in history. Its immense size and lifting capacity allowed it to carry up to 1,700 pounds of bombs alongside defensive machine guns, making it uniquely formidable in the early years of the conflict.

Operating from early 1915, the Ilya Muromets fleet flew over four hundred combat sorties against German and Austro-Hungarian positions. Their defensive armament and robust construction meant they rarely fell to enemy fighters; over the entire war, only a single aircraft was definitively lost to hostile aircraft. Following the Russian Revolution, surviving examples were briefly used for mail and transport before the type was finally retired in 1922.
